script.speaker: Receptionist
script.textEn: Good afternoon, City Medical Center. How may I help you?

script.speaker: Patient
script.textEn: Hello, I'd like to make an appointment with Dr. Chen, please.

script.speaker: Receptionist
script.textEn: Of course. Are you a new or returning patient?

script.speaker: Patient
script.textEn: I'm a new patient. I've been having terrible headaches this week.

script.speaker: Receptionist
script.textEn: I'm sorry to hear that. Dr. Chen has an opening tomorrow at half past nine, or Friday at three.

script.speaker: Patient
script.textEn: Tomorrow at nine thirty would be perfect.

script.speaker: Receptionist
script.textEn: May I have your full name and date of birth, please?

script.speaker: Patient
script.textEn: My name is Daniel Park, and I was born on March the twelfth, 1998.

script.speaker: Receptionist
script.textEn: Thank you, Mr. Park. Please bring your insurance card and arrive fifteen minutes early.

script.speaker: Patient
script.textEn: Do I need to fast before the appointment?

script.speaker: Receptionist
script.textEn: No fasting is required, but please bring a list of any medication you take.

script.speaker: Patient
script.textEn: Got it. Thank you very much for your help.

questions.explanationVi: Dòng l8: 'My name is Daniel Park'.

questions.explanationVi: Dòng l9: 'arrive fifteen minutes early'.

questions.explanationVi: Dòng l11: 'No fasting is required' — thông tin này sai.

script.speaker: Interviewer

script.speaker: Candidate

script.speaker: Interviewer

script.speaker: Candidate

script.speaker: Interviewer

script.speaker: Candidate

script.speaker: Candidate

script.speaker: Interviewer

script.speaker: Candidate

title: Flight Delay at the Airport
titleVi: Chuyến bay bị hoãn ở sân bay

script.speaker: Agent
script.textEn: Good evening, how can I help you?

script.speaker: Passenger
script.textEn: Hi, I'm flying to Singapore on flight SQ-618. I'd like to check in.

script.speaker: Agent
script.textEn: May I see your passport, please?

script.speaker: Passenger
script.textEn: Here you go. Is the flight on time?

script.speaker: Agent
script.textEn: I'm afraid there's a two-hour delay due to bad weather.

script.speaker: Passenger
script.textEn: Oh no! What time does it depart now?

script.speaker: Agent
script.textEn: The new departure time is quarter to twelve, from gate B7.

script.speaker: Passenger
script.textEn: Do I need to do anything, or just wait at the gate?

script.speaker: Agent
script.textEn: Just wait at the gate. We'll call boarding thirty minutes before departure.

script.speaker: Passenger
script.textEn: Can I get a meal voucher for the delay?

script.speaker: Agent
script.textEn: Yes, here's a voucher worth twenty dollars for the food court on level two.

script.speaker: Passenger
script.textEn: That's very kind. Thank you for your help.

title: Lecture: The History of Money
titleVi: Bài giảng: Lịch sử tiền tệ

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.textEn: Good morning, everyone. Today we'll look at how money came to exist.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.textEn: Before money, people used barter, trading goods directly, like exchanging wheat for cloth.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.textEn: The problem with barter was finding someone who wanted exactly what you had.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.textEn: Around 3000 BC, the Mesopotamians began using silver bars as a standard of value.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.textEn: The first real coins appeared in Lydia, in modern day Turkey, about 600 BC.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.textEn: These coins were made of electrum, a natural mixture of gold and silver.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.textEn: Paper money came much later, invented in China during the Tang Dynasty, around the seventh century.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.textEn: Interestingly, paper money was first used as a promise to pay, not as money itself.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.textEn: In 1971, the US dollar left the gold standard, and most currencies became fiat money.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.textEn: Fiat money has value simply because governments say it does.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.textEn: Today, digital payments are replacing cash in many countries, especially in Scandinavia.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.textEn: Cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin represent the latest experiment in what money can be.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.textEn: Next week, we'll examine how central banks control the money supply. Thank you.

questions.question: What was the main problem with barter?
options: Finding someone who wanted exactly what you had
Goods were too heavy to carry
questions.correctAnswer: Finding someone who wanted exactly what you had
questions.explanationVi: Dòng l3 nêu đúng vấn đề này.

questions.question: The first coins were made of ___
questions.explanationVi: Dòng l6: 'These coins were made of electrum'.

questions.question: Paper money was invented in China during the ___
questions.explanationVi: Dòng l7: 'invented in China during the Tang Dynasty'.

questions.question: In 1971, the US dollar left the gold standard.
questions.explanationVi: Dòng l9 ghi đúng như vậy.

questions.question: Cash has completely disappeared in Scandinavia.
questions.explanationVi: Dòng l11: 'replacing cash' — đang dần thay thế, chưa biến mất hoàn toàn.

title: Seminar: Artificial Intelligence in Healthcare
titleVi: Hội thảo: Trí tuệ nhân tạo trong y tế

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.textEn: Welcome to today's seminar on artificial intelligence in medicine.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.textEn: AI is already helping doctors detect diseases earlier than ever before.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.textEn: For example, deep learning models can now spot lung cancer in X-rays with remarkable accuracy.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.textEn: One major advantage is speed. An AI system can analyze thousands of scans in a single hour.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.textEn: However, there are serious concerns about patient privacy and data security.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.textEn: Hospitals must ensure that sensitive medical records are properly protected.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.textEn: Another challenge is bias. If training data lacks diversity, the AI may misdiagnose certain groups.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.textEn: Researchers are working on explainable AI, which can show doctors how it reached a conclusion.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.textEn: Importantly, experts agree that AI should assist doctors, not replace them.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.textEn: The human touch, empathy and judgment, remains essential in patient care.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.textEn: By 2030, analysts predict that most hospitals will use AI tools in daily practice.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.textEn: In our next session, we'll look at AI applications in drug discovery.

script.speaker: Lecturer
script.textEn: Thank you for your attention.

questions.question: What is one major advantage of AI in medicine?
questions.explanationVi: Dòng l4: AI 'can analyze thousands of scans in a single hour' — lợi thế về tốc độ.

questions.question: AI models can spot ___ in X-rays
questions.explanationVi: Dòng l3: 'spot lung cancer in X-rays'.

questions.question: AI should replace doctors completely.
questions.explanationVi: Dòng l9: 'AI should assist doctors, not replace them' — ngược lại.

questions.question: What does 'explainable AI' do?
options: Shows doctors how it reached a conclusion
questions.correctAnswer: Shows doctors how it reached a conclusion
questions.explanationVi: Dòng l8 giải thích đúng như vậy.

questions.question: Most hospitals already use AI tools in daily practice.
questions.explanationVi: Dòng l11: đây là dự đoán 'By 2030' — tương lai, chưa phải hiện tại.

title: Briefing: Campus Safety for New Students
titleVi: Hướng dẫn an toàn khuôn viên cho tân sinh viên

script.speaker: Officer
script.textEn: Welcome, new students. I'm Officer Rivera from campus security.

script.speaker: Officer
script.textEn: First, always lock your dorm room, even if you're just going down the hall.

script.speaker: Officer
script.textEn: The emergency number on campus is extension 4911, available twenty four hours a day.

script.speaker: Officer
script.textEn: If you feel unsafe walking at night, our SafeRide shuttle runs until 2 AM.

script.speaker: Officer
script.textEn: You can request a pickup by calling the security office or using the campus app.

script.speaker: Officer
script.textEn: Never share your student ID card with anyone. It also works as your library card.

script.speaker: Officer
script.textEn: The library closes at midnight on weekdays and at ten PM on weekends.

script.speaker: Officer
script.textEn: Report any suspicious activity immediately. It's always better to be cautious.

script.speaker: Officer
script.textEn: We also offer free self defense classes every Thursday evening in the sports center.

script.speaker: Officer
script.textEn: Registration for the classes opens on the first of September.

script.speaker: Officer
script.textEn: Finally, sign up for emergency text alerts on the university website.

script.speaker: Officer
script.textEn: Stay safe, and enjoy your time here. Thank you.

questions.question: The campus emergency number is extension ___
questions.explanationVi: Dòng l3: 'extension 4911'.

questions.question: The SafeRide shuttle runs until ___
questions.explanationVi: Dòng l4: 'runs until 2 AM'.

questions.question: Students may share their ID cards with close friends.
questions.explanationVi: Dòng l6: 'Never share your student ID card with anyone' — cấm tuyệt đối.

questions.question: When do the self-defense classes take place?
questions.explanationVi: Dòng l9: 'every Thursday evening'.

questions.question: How can students sign up for emergency text alerts?
questions.explanationVi: Dòng l11: 'sign up for emergency text alerts on the university website'.

title: Guided Tour: Royal Botanical Gardens
titleVi: Tham quan: Vườn thực vật Hoàng gia

script.speaker: Guide
script.textEn: Hello everyone, and welcome to the Royal Botanical Gardens.

script.speaker: Guide
script.textEn: Our gardens cover over two hundred acres and house more than ten thousand plant species.

script.speaker: Guide
script.textEn: We'll begin at the Palm House, built in 1848, which contains tropical plants from five continents.

script.speaker: Guide
script.textEn: Next, we'll visit the Desert Garden, home to the world's oldest cactus collection.

script.speaker: Guide
script.textEn: Please do not touch the plants, as many are rare and extremely fragile.

script.speaker: Guide
script.textEn: The Orchid Pavilion is our most photographed spot, especially during the spring festival.

script.speaker: Guide
script.textEn: Lunch is available at the Garden Cafe, which serves only locally grown produce.

script.speaker: Guide
script.textEn: The tour takes approximately ninety minutes, and we'll finish at the main gate.

script.speaker: Guide
script.textEn: If you have questions, please save them for our stops. The paths can be quite narrow.

script.speaker: Guide
script.textEn: Photography is allowed everywhere except inside the Orchid Pavilion.

script.speaker: Guide
script.textEn: Finally, the gift shop offers seeds from our own gardens, perfect for souvenirs.

script.speaker: Guide
script.textEn: Let's get started. Follow me, please!

questions.question: The gardens cover over ___ acres
questions.explanationVi: Dòng l2: 'cover over two hundred acres'.

questions.question: The Palm House was built in ___
questions.explanationVi: Dòng l3: 'built in 1848'.

questions.question: Visitors may touch the plants in the Desert Garden.
questions.explanationVi: Dòng l5: 'do not touch the plants' — cấm chạm vào cây.

questions.question: Where is photography NOT allowed?
questions.explanationVi: Dòng l10: 'except inside the Orchid Pavilion'.

questions.question: The tour lasts the whole day.
questions.explanationVi: Dòng l8: tour chỉ 'approximately ninety minutes', không phải cả ngày.
